$comment: Contract Verification Aggregation SEP (draft) — the aggregated view across verifiers. Closed for a producer; a consumer validates with additionalProperties relaxed. An entry here is a RELAY: it keeps every field the verifier published, including ones this schema does not name, which is why `verification` is the one object in the SEP that is deliberately open.
title: Contract Verification Aggregate (Aggregation SEP 1.0)
description: The body of GET /v1/wasms/{wasm_hash} on an aggregator. Assembled per request — no static file corresponds to it, and `unavailable_verifiers` describes this fetch. An aggregator relays and does not judge: entries are never merged into one verdict, and `agreement` is a description of how they relate, not a conclusion.

schema.description: The document type. Every Results SEP document names its type here beside its version.

schema_version.description: MAJOR.MINOR of this envelope, and of the envelope only. A relayed entry carries the version of the document it was read from in its own `schema_version`; an aggregator that re-versioned entries would be a silent translator.

wasm_hash.description: The Wasm hash this view is about. Lowercase hex SHA-256.

updated_at.description: When the AGGREGATOR assembled this view — never a verifier's own publication time. A consumer wanting the latter reads the entry's `processed_at`.

source_code_verifications.description: One headline entry per verifier that answered. Empty is meaningful and distinct from `unavailable_verifiers` being non-empty: nobody has a result, versus we could not reach some.

unavailable_verifiers.description: Always present, empty when nothing failed. Omitting it would conflate 'no verifier has a result' with 'we could not reach some', which is the one distinction an aggregator must not blur.

agreement.description: Descriptive, never a verdict. `single` rather than `unanimous_verified` for one entry, because unanimity among one overstates. Disagreement is reported and not adjudicated.

verifier.description: A verifier's identity. Exactly one field identifies: `url`, the result root. `name` is what the verifier calls itself — self-claimed, preferred, never authoritative, and present to be displayed rather than keyed on. A reader that wants a name it can hold someone to derives one from `url` (its certificate, the reader's own list); that is a UI concern and not this document's.

url.description: The verifier's result root, and its identity. Two entries in one Trusted Verifiers List cannot share it, because the same result root IS the same verifier. Compared after normalising: scheme and host lowercased, one trailing `/` dropped, path kept and case-sensitive — without a stated rule two implementations disagree on whether `https://v.example/` and `https://v.example` are one verifier or two.

name.description: Self-claimed. Display it, do not key on it, and do not read it as an endorsement by whoever relayed it.

relayed_verification.description: One verifier's entry, relayed. DELIBERATELY OPEN (`additionalProperties` unconstrained): a verifier may publish fields this version does not name, and an aggregator that dropped them would be editing the claim it is passing on. `verifier` is the peer's own block, unchanged — an aggregator does not substitute its own label for the verifier's, and needs no second identity block and no aggregator-local id, because the result root identifies without anyone asserting anything.

verifier.description: The peer's own identity block, relayed unchanged. `url` identifies; `name` is self-claimed.

schema_version.description: The version of the document this entry was read from. Absent when the aggregator retained the entry before it recorded versions.

status.description: The verifier's verdict. An aggregator that does not recognise a value serves it as `unverified` rather than dropping the entry or rejecting the document.

processed_at.description: When the VERIFIER reached this verdict. The answer to 'when was this verified?' — `updated_at` above is not.

retrieved_at.description: When the aggregator last successfully read this entry. Present only on a retained copy: a stale result is served honestly, labelled with its age, rather than withheld.

results_urls.description: Relayed unchanged, sha256 included — this is what lets a consumer bypass the aggregator and verify any single entry at its source.

unavailable_verifier.description: A verifier that could not contribute to THIS view, identified by its result root exactly as a contributing one is — so a consumer lines the two lists up on one field rather than two vocabularies. `name` is whatever the aggregator's own list calls it: there is no peer document to relay, so it is a label and claims no more.

name.description: The aggregator's own label. Not identity.

reason.description: Every value is something that happened to a request the aggregator made: `refused` means its own policy rejected the destination before any request went out. There is deliberately no value for "not asked yet" — an aggregator that has not read its list cannot answer at all, and says so with a 5xx (see the SEP's Errors section) rather than serving a 200 that looks like an answer.

error.description: Operator-facing detail. Not part of any contract.
